title: Capture residual backlog in planner and remove legacy checklist files
summary: Audit legacy backlog files against code + planner, migrate only real gaps into planner tasks, then switch docs/process to planner-only.
description:
This phase converts the repository from mixed backlog management (`CHECKLIST.md` + `BACKLOG.md` + planner) to planner-only governance.

Current implementation state and evidence:
- `AGENTS.md` still hard-requires `CHECKLIST.md` and instructs contributors to keep it updated.
- `PROJECT.md` and `ROADMAP.md` still describe a mandatory checklist process.
- The planner already owns real execution state (`P034` in progress with `T136` and `T137`; `P035` done), so legacy markdown backlogs now create drift.
- Confirmed real gaps remain outside the planner: feature discuss flow missing; `/handoff` delete missing; orphan cleanup missing; requirements page missing; `PlanStoreError` diagnostics too shallow; project description editor missing; multi-harness docs/schema missing; Zed integration missing; Pi upstream issue not filed.

Implementation work in this phase:
1. Create explicit planner tasks for each still-open real gap, with code references and acceptance notes.
2. Add one migration task that rewrites process docs (`AGENTS.md`, `PROJECT.md`, `ROADMAP.md`) from checklist-backed governance to planner-only governance.
3. Delete `CHECKLIST.md` and `BACKLOG.md` only after every real open item has been captured in planner tasks.
4. Re-render generated planner docs after the planner data changes.

Behaviors to preserve:
- do not duplicate existing open planner work (`T136`, `T137` remain in `P034`).
- keep the planner as the only source of truth for open work after migration.
- keep the core harness-agnostic; this cleanup is governance/documentation plus planner structure, not a Pi-only shortcut.

tasks.notes:
Captured upstream Pi follow-up for the session_start prompt rendering bug.

Diagnosis from packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:799-855:
- `ctx.ui.input()` and `ctx.ui.select()` do NOT render when called inside the `session_start` hook of an NPM-loaded ESM Pi extension.
- The prompt hangs invisible; if wrapped with a timeout, it expires after the safety net without user interaction.
- This only affects NPM-installed ESM extensions; local source-loaded extensions render the prompts correctly.
- The practical workaround implemented in Agent Plan: remove ALL blocking startup prompts from `session_start`, keep the planner disabled by default, and require an explicit `/planner load` command (which runs outside `session_start`) to enable the planner and start the web UI.

Upstream issue to file against Pi:
- Repository: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (or the appropriate Pi extension runtime repo)
- Title: `ctx.ui.input()/select() do not render during session_start for NPM-loaded ESM extensions`
- Labels: bug, extensions, ui
- Body should include:
  - Pi version and Node version (currently Node 25.4.0)
  - Extension loaded via `pi install npm:@agent-plan/pi-adapter`
  - Code snippet: `pi.on("session_start", async (_event, ctx) => { await ctx.ui.input({ message: "Enable?" }); })`
  - Expected: prompt renders and resolves
  - Actual: prompt never renders; the call hangs until timeout
  - Workaround: defer interactive prompts to a later hook or command handler

This task is now the source of truth for tracking the upstream issue. The legacy CHECKLIST.md notes about the prompt freeze are superseded. No Agent Plan code changes needed; the local workaround is already in place.

tasks.title: Apply pattern to all status headers (not just terminal)
tasks.description:
After scoping the pattern to the header, the pattern only appears for closed/canceled/rejected. Other statuses (in-progress, started, deferred, blocked, waiting) have no pattern on the header because `statusPatternClass` only renders for terminal states.

Fix: use `patternClass(status)` from display-status-tokens.ts everywhere a pattern is needed on a header. This maps to the existing `.status-pattern-*` CSS classes (dashed, pulse, stripe, hatch, crosshatch) which cover all statuses that have a pattern.

tasks.title: Map borders for all statuses + reduce rejected intensity
tasks.description:
After scoping the pattern to the header, the user wants visible borders for ALL statuses on the outer container (not just closed/canceled/rejected). Also reduce the rejected pattern intensity so the badge text is readable.

Plan:
1. Update `statusBorderClass(status)` to always return a class for every status (no empty return).
2. Add `.ap-status-border-*` CSS rules for ALL statuses: planned, started, in-progress, waiting, blocked, deferred, done, closed, canceled, rejected.
   - For `started` and `deferred` and `waiting`: dashed border style.
   - For `planned`: dashed border (placeholder).
   - For `in-progress`, `done`, `closed`, `canceled`, `rejected`, `blocked`: solid border.
3. Reduce the rejected pattern intensity in `.status-pattern-crosshatch` from 14% to 8% so the badge text is readable on patterned backgrounds.
4. Verify the work-tree-row container always has a colored border.

tasks.title: Unify border styles + visible backgrounds for all statuses
tasks.description:
Fix inconsistencies between task (statusSurfaceClass) and phase/feature (statusBorderClass) border styles, and make background tints visible enough.

Issues:
1. Inconsistency: task planned uses solid border (from .ap-status-surface-planned), phase planned uses dashed border (from .ap-status-border-planned). They should be uniform.
2. Started same problem as Done/Planned: borders not visible enough.
3. In Progress has border but no background tint (6% alpha too subtle).
4. Done border too faint (32% opacity), feature F001 has no visible border at all.

Fix:
1. Update .ap-status-surface-planned/started/waiting/deferred to use dashed border-style matching the border-only classes.
2. Increase background tint for in-progress, started, done (5-6% → 10-12%) for visible presence.
3. Increase Done border color intensity (32% → 50%) for visibility.
4. Ensure In Progress has both visible border and visible tint.

tasks.title: Use full surface for feature/phase container + no-pattern override
tasks.description:
Force feature and phase containers to use the full surface treatment (background tint + border) via statusSurfaceClass, instead of the border-only statusBorderClass. For closed/canceled/rejected, add an override class `ap-status-surface-no-pattern` to strip the pattern from the container so it only appears on the inner header (not on the expansion area below). Pattern-only signals remain on the inner header via patternClass.

Also bumped alpha levels in .ap-status-border-* (kept as a fallback) to 50-60% for stronger visibility.

tasks.title: Force visible borders: bump alpha 70-75% and 1.5px width
tasks.description: User frustration: borders still not visible. Push alpha to 70-75% (was 50-60%) and border-width to 1.5px (was 1px) for all .ap-status-surface-* rules. Bumped background tint 10% → 14-16% so the presence is even more visible. Bumped closed/canceled/rejected pattern intensity 22→22% but kept tint at 8-10% so badge stays readable.

tasks.title: Refactor: single source of truth for status visual config (bg, fg, border, pattern)
tasks.description:
Refactor the status surface treatment to use a single visual config map in display-status-tokens.ts. The CSS for .ap-status-surface-* (10 scattered rules with bg/border/widht/pattern) is replaced with ONE CSS rule that consumes CSS variables. The variables are populated via inline style from a JS map (STATUS_VISUAL).

After this refactor:
- Adding a new status = ONE entry in STATUS_VISUAL.
- Tweaking visibility = ONE number in bgAlpha/borderAlpha.
- Tweaking pattern intensity = ONE number in patternAlpha.
- No more duplication of CSS rules.

Plan:
1. Add STATUS_VISUAL map in display-status-tokens.ts with per-status config: bgAlpha, borderAlpha, borderStyle, borderWidth, patternKind, patternAlpha, patternDensity, fgAlpha.
2. Add statusStyleVars(status) helper that returns inline CSS properties for the --status-* variables.
3. Replace .ap-status-surface-* scattered CSS rules with a single .ap-status-surface rule that uses the variables.
4. Keep .ap-status-surface-no-pattern as a single override.
5. Update work-tree-rows.tsx (FeatureTreeRow, PhaseTreeRow, TaskTreeRow) to use statusStyleVars(status) on the container.
6. Optionally: refactor the badge to use the same statusStyleVars for fg/bg.
7. Verify build/check.
